svg.title: Architecture comparison poster: six storage architectures
svg.desc: Six panels, each with a mini-diagram and three bullets for strength, wall and example products. Scale-up dual-controller: two controllers with mirrored NVRAM over one shared drive shelf. Scale-out shared-nothing: nodes that each own CPU and drives joined by an east-west network. DASE: stateless compute nodes meshed over an NVMe-oF fabric to shared enclosures of SCM and QLC flash. Parallel file system: a client fetches a layout from a metadata server, then stripes data directly to several data servers. Object: stateless S3 gateways, an index mapping keys to fragments, and data nodes holding erasure-coded fragments. SDS and HCI: nodes that each run applications, storage software and local drives, pooled over the LAN. Everpure products are marked in each panel. The same content appears as Table 60.3.
svg.text: Architecture poster: six ways to build a storage system
Logical views, not to scale. Each panel: how it is wired, what it is good at, where it hits a wall, who ships it.
Strength: fewest hops, sub-ms block; a
controller swap is a planned failover
Wall: one controller pair's CPU and memory;
federating pairs is not one bigger system.
HPE Alletra MP B10000; IBM FlashSystem.
Clients: any node is an entry point
Strength: capacity and bandwidth grow node
by node; placement is computed; self-heals.
NVMe-oF fabric: every node, every SSD
stateless CNodes above, shared SCM + QLC below
Strength: compute and media scale separately;
Wall: every I/O crosses the back-end fabric;
an enclosure is a failure domain; big minimum.
Examples: VAST Data; NetApp AFX; HPE
Alletra MP X10000. Everpure: none (EXA is
Strength: clients stripe directly across many
Wall: metadata and small files; proprietary
clients tie upgrades to kernel builds.
Wall: object count, small objects, LIST and
tail latency; no POSIX or in-place edits.
Examples: AWS S3, MinIO AIStor, Cloudian,
Pooled across nodes over the LAN
Strength: commodity servers or cloud; storage
and compute run as one estate.
Wall: coupled scaling strands compute or
capacity; vendor does not control the media.
Blue bold marks Everpure products. Placement follows Chapters 14–19 and 24; the seventh row of Chapter 24's matrix, cloud block
storage (EBS-style), is SDS run by a hyperscaler and is left off the poster. Original drawing, Chapter 60.
